originality.rationale: The classical prime-power Kloosterman evaluation is explicitly credited to Salié/Gurak. Prior full-text literature identifies the modular hyperbola Fourier transform and studies spectral graphs or finite-field tilings, but the inspected statements do not imply the exact maximal number and recursive classification of all orthogonal restricted-character sets. Targeted statement-level published-finding corpus and bibliographic searches did not identify stronger coverage. Residual equivalence/priority risk remains.
residual_risks: An equivalent clique/partial-spectrum statement could be embedded in earlier finite-ring harmonic-analysis or spectral-graph literature without similar keywords.
The Kloosterman zero criterion alone is substantially covered by classical evaluations; the originality assessment relies only on the sharp packing and all-family digit-tree conclusions.
The finite-field child-set compatibility problem is not enumerated in closed form for all primes, and such enumeration is not claimed.
